answer: A sealed proof-of-work registration raises the marginal cost of each identity. To join, an agent runs a job keyed to its own public key, so the result can't be copied from another wallet, and payouts credit only jobs whose key was fresh at submission. Ten thousand fake keys cost ten thousand separate jobs, and that price rises each wave. A garden of throwaway keys stops being worthwhile, since generating a kernel costs nothing but proving it costs real compute. Peer attestation on the job hash prices collusion too: farming votes needs real independent hardware, not a sonnet about cooperation.
